seo.title: Homeless help in Cardiff - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help for people who are homeless or at risk in Cardiff: emergency housing, outreach, food, health care, benefits, work and specialist support.

content.text: Tell the worker where you are tonight, where you usually sleep, your age, whether children are with you, and whether pregnancy, disability, illness, domestic abuse, immigration restrictions or a pet affects what is safe. Ask for Welsh-language support or an interpreter if needed.

call Housing Options and say clearly that you are homeless today or at risk of losing your home. Ask to make a homelessness application. If you have nowhere tonight, call the out-of-hours number after the daytime service closes. Temporary accommodation depends on an assessment.

Call for immediate violence, serious injury, overdose, breathing difficulty, loss of consciousness, fire or another life-threatening emergency. Give the exact location or nearest landmark first. If you cannot speak on a mobile call to police, listen and press 55 when prompted.

with the location and description of an adult sleeping outside. Reports go to local outreach; neither service is an emergency line or bed-booking service. Call 999 for immediate danger or a child at risk.

items.name: The Wallich Rough Sleepers Intervention Team

content.text: The team works daily from 7am–3pm and checks known rough-sleeping locations. It can provide breakfast, hot drinks, sleeping bags, warm clothing and toiletries, plus housing, health, benefits and substance-use referrals.

Salvation Army outreach normally operates 5pm–9pm daily with food, hot drinks, emergency care and access routes to accommodation. When the Severe Weather Emergency Protocol is active, call Outreach on
RISE can help all genders with safety planning and practical help; refuge or another safe place depends on assessment and availability. Do not return for papers or belongings if it is unsafe.

categories.title: 2. Day centres, shelter pathways and housing support

content.text: Huggard Buildings, Hansen Street, Cardiff CF10 5DW; use CF10 5JZ for sat nav

Open daily 8:30am–6pm for adults needing food, warmth or a safe space. Services include advice, free and low-cost meals, clothing, showers and laundry. Emergency beds are allocated by referral; visiting the day centre does not guarantee a bed.

Monday–Friday 8:30am–10am by appointment and 10am–3pm as a drop-in. For adults experiencing homelessness. Housing and benefits advice, support to secure or maintain accommodation, mental-health and substance-use referrals, showers, laundry, practical supplies, training and learning.
Central Library Hub, The Hayes, Cardiff CF10 1FL
. Open Monday–Thursday 9am–4:30pm and Friday 9am–4pm, without appointment.

For people who do not have a local connection to Cardiff, the service explores a safe return or another positive accommodation route. It should not replace an urgent homelessness application when you have nowhere safe.

Housing-related support for eligible Cardiff residents aged 16+ who are at risk of homelessness or starting a tenancy and face an additional barrier. A social worker, housing officer, health professional or Hub officer must refer you; self-referrals are not accepted.
. Volunteers normally work in the city centre Friday and Saturday 10pm–4am.
They can listen, help people reach clothing, hostel and housing services, and sometimes accompany someone to an appointment. They are not an emergency accommodation provider.
Huggard Buildings, Hansen Street, Cardiff CF10 5DW
Anyone in need of food, warmth or a safe space can attend daily 8:30am–6pm. Free and low-cost meals are available; ask on arrival what is being served and whether capacity is limited.
The Dusty Forge, 460 Cowbridge Road West, Ely, Cardiff CF5 5BZ
A free, meat-free community meal is normally served Monday at 6:30pm. Everyone is welcome and no voucher or referral is normally needed. Children must be accompanied by an adult.
Wyndham Street Centre, 3–5 Wyndham Street, Riverside, Cardiff CF11 6DQ
A free, meat-free community meal is normally served Wednesday at 6:30pm. Everyone is welcome and no voucher or referral is normally required.

Eight distribution centres operate on different days, including City Church, Woodville Christian Centre, Grangetown Baptist Church and St Saviour's Church. Do not go to the Titan Road warehouse for food; it does not distribute parcels.

Weekday drop-in access normally runs 10am–3pm. Ask about showers, laundry and practical provisions. Morning access before 10am is by appointment.

items.name: Cardiff and Vale Health Inclusion Service

content.text: Walk-in homeless-outreach clinics are for people who live in hostels, use day services or sleep outside. No appointment is required. Ask hostel or day-centre staff for current clinic times, or ask Cardiff Outreach on
Clinics can include nursing, GP assessment, health checks, vaccination, sexual and reproductive health, eye care and dental referrals. Times and locations change with outreach demand.

items.name: Register with a GP without an address or ID

content.text: Anyone can register with a GP practice in Wales. A fixed address and identification are not required. Prescriptions are free for people registered with a GP in Wales, and a free interpreter can be requested.
A practice may refuse only if its list is full or you live outside its area. Ask for an explanation if refused and call NHS Wales Shared Services on
for Contractor Services if you cannot find a practice.

, 24 hours. A clinician assesses the problem and, when appropriate, books an emergency clinic. Call 999 for severe swelling affecting breathing or swallowing, uncontrollable bleeding or major facial injury.
and press 2 for urgent mental-health advice and support. Call 999 if life is in immediate danger.

For single adults accessing homelessness services. The team can provide rapid assessment and support involving mental-health workers, substance-use specialists, nursing, counselling, occupational therapy, dietetics, social work, women's specialists and employment support.
Ask Housing Options, Outreach, Huggard or The Wallich for access. This is not a public emergency department.
. CADT provides practical guidance, needs assessment, community-care advice and one-to-one counselling for people affected by alcohol or drug use.

items.name: CAVDAS homelessness outreach and rapid prescribing

content.text: Cardiff and Vale Drug and Alcohol Service works with the council's homeless multidisciplinary team. Support includes outreach, counselling, harm reduction, take-home naloxone, blood-borne-virus and sexual-health screening, and rapid access to opioid-substitution prescribing for eligible people.
Ask an outreach or homelessness worker for access. Prescribing requires clinical assessment.

categories.title: 7. Toilets, internet, charging and warm spaces

items.name: Central Library Hub / Hyb y Llyfrgell Ganolog

content.text: Free Wi-Fi, public computers, telephones, document scanning, library services and a reading and relaxation area. The Hub also hosts Money Advice, Into Work, Citizens Advice and council services on scheduled days.
Check the live Hub page for opening hours and appointment requirements. Printing and photocopying may cost.

Libraries offer free Wi-Fi except at Tongwynlais, free public computers at listed branches and public printing. A library card and PIN are needed to log into a computer; ask staff how to join if you have no fixed address or identification.

Cardiff Hubs have publicly available toilets, and visitors are welcome to use them without accessing another service. The council also lists public and Community Toilet Scheme locations. Check accessibility and current opening times before a long journey.
Cardiff Hubs and partner venues provide free warm places, company and access to advice during cold periods. Locations and seasonal opening times change.

An Emergency Assistance Payment may help an eligible person aged 16+ in extreme hardship with food, gas, electricity, clothing or emergency travel after an unexpected crisis. It is a grant, not a loan. Apply online or call
You must live in Wales and have no other money available. Limits apply to repeat awards, and ongoing bills are not covered. A decision or payment is not guaranteed immediately.
. Free help with budgeting, income maximisation, benefits and debt. The team or a Hub may also assess emergency food vouchers and help with a DAF application.

items.name: Universal Credit without a fixed address

content.text: You can claim while rough sleeping, sofa surfing or staying in a hostel. With permission, use a trusted person's, hostel, day-centre or Jobcentre address. If you lack identification, a bank account, phone, email or National Insurance number, say so: alternatives may be possible.

Tell your work coach about homelessness, mental ill health or recovery needs and ask whether the claimant commitment should change temporarily. Supported or temporary accommodation may use Housing Benefit separately.
Universal Credit guidance for homeless people

items.name: Benefits and council services at a Hub

content.text: Hubs can help with Housing Benefit, council tax, the housing waiting list, online applications and document scanning. Service days and appointment rules vary. Central Library Hub and several neighbourhood Hubs also host Money Advice and Into Work.

categories.title: 9. Work, training and travel to an interview

content.text: Free help with CVs, applications, job search, interviews, Universal Credit, skills training, volunteering and placements. Eligible people may receive help with childcare, travel or other work costs. Ask at Central Library Hub or another participating Hub.
Confirm funding before buying anything; support is assessed and not automatic.
The weekday Solutions Service offers access to training, learning and development alongside housing and welfare support. Drop-in normally runs 10am–3pm; morning access is by appointment.
Huggard Buildings, Hansen Street, Cardiff CF10 5DW
Adults using the day centre can ask about support, advice and development opportunities alongside immediate practical help. Attendance does not create a job or housing placement.
Use the official Find a Job service and postcode search for a current Jobcentre. A Jobcentre can help with Universal Credit, work-coach appointments and National Insurance questions.
Free careers information and guidance for people in Wales, including job search, training, qualifications, CVs and interviews. Ask for telephone or online help if travel is difficult.

Huggard states that people believed to use its services may receive mail care of the centre. Ask first about permission, the exact address format, collection rules and how long post is kept. The centre cannot confirm to another person whether someone uses the service.
send post or leave identification, papers or belongings without explicit permission.

Check old payslips, benefit letters, a tax account or UKVI account first. You may start work before receiving a number if you can prove the right to work, and do not need one to start a benefit claim.
Apply for or find a number

British and Irish citizens may use an eligible passport or a birth or adoption certificate together with an official document showing the National Insurance number. Other people may use a share code or eligible immigration documents.
Do not pay an unofficial agent. Ask Cardiff Advice Service or a regulated adviser if status is unclear.

items.name: Replace a birth certificate or get passport advice

content.text: Order certificates through the General Register Office or relevant register office; fees apply. Contact HM Passport Office before paying if documents, referees or delivery are difficult. A charity may help with an application but cannot guarantee the fee.

Central Library Hub and neighbourhood Hubs provide computers, scanning and public telephones; printing may cost. No verified open-access public luggage-storage service was found. Ask Housing Options, Huggard or The Wallich about a safe option before leaving belongings.

categories.title: 11. Housing law, debt and legal advice

content.text: Free, independent advice about homelessness, eviction, rent or mortgage arrears, disrepair and housing rights in Wales. Shelter Cymru does not operate accommodation, kitchens or emergency beds.

Citizens Advice and Speakeasy provide free, independent and confidential advice through Cardiff Hubs on benefits, debt, housing, employment, immigration, discrimination, family and consumer problems. Locations and opening times vary.
. Office open Monday–Friday 10am–1pm; most contact is by phone or email, with some face-to-face appointments.

Free specialist advice on homelessness, eviction, disrepair, benefits, debt and employment law for Cardiff and Vale residents. The team normally aims to connect a caller with an adviser within two working days.

Contact Housing Options before leaving a tenancy. The council can discuss rent arrears, debt, landlord relations, deposits, rent in advance and alternatives. In most cases a private renter has the right to remain until the legal process reaches a court bailiff warrant.

content.text: Specialist support concerning domestic abuse, sexual violence, stalking, exploitation, trafficking, forced marriage and honour-based abuse. RISE can help with safety, securing a current home or finding another safe place. Refuge is subject to assessment and availability.

Social care does not replace a homelessness application. Contact both services when care needs affect safe accommodation.

People experiencing homelessness can use the UK help form to ask about free volunteer veterinary care. Eligibility and local coverage are assessed. StreetVet is not an emergency service and does not cover existing bills or provide fostering.

The UK-wide scheme helps eligible dog owners with veterinary costs and finding dog-friendly services. A participating homelessness service may need to apply. Assessment applies; existing bills and every procedure are not automatically covered.

items.name: Tell every service about your pet

content.text: Tell Housing Options and each referrer the species, size, health, behaviour and vaccination status. Ask about pet-friendly accommodation or temporary animal care before accepting or rejecting an offer. Do not abandon an animal or arrive at a hostel expecting admission.
, Monday–Friday 7am–6pm. Use the official site for routes, timetables, fares and live disruption. Different operators may require different tickets.

Use the official journey planner for trains and participating bus routes. Ask a housing, health, council or Jobcentre worker before an essential appointment whether travel can be authorised; help is not automatic.

items.name: Travel for interviews or a new job

content.text: Cardiff Into Work may help eligible jobseekers with travel and other work costs. Ask and obtain approval before paying. A Jobcentre work coach may separately consider agreed employment costs.

An integrated ticket connects a Transport for Wales train from Cardiff Central to Rhoose Cardiff International Airport station and the 905 bus to the terminal. Current total journey time is about 48 minutes. Check the day's timetable, connection and fare before travel; the airport is not a shelter.

items.name: Taking an animal on Cardiff Bus

content.text: Assistance dogs travel when space is available. One well-behaved dog or small animal may travel at the driver's discretion, under control and off the seats. Ask before boarding; transport permission does not mean accommodation will accept the animal.
Services change. Please report a closed service, wrong detail or safer alternative through the project repository. Do not send private medical, immigration or housing documents.
